title: Stretch Summing to a Multiple of K
statement:
You get an array nums of non-negative integers and a positive integer k. Decide whether there is a contiguous stretch of at least two elements whose sum is a multiple of k.

0 counts as a multiple of every k. Return true or false.

examples.why: The 6 on its own is a multiple, but a single element is too short. The stretches of two or more sum to 7, 7 and 8.
The sum is 0, which is a multiple of 5.

hints: The sum of nums[i..j] is prefix[j + 1] − prefix[i]. When is a difference a multiple of k?
Exactly when both prefix sums leave the same remainder after dividing by k.
Walk once, keeping a map from remainder to the earliest prefix index with that remainder (remainder 0 at index 0 to start). A repeat at least two positions later is the answer.

explain.intuition:
A stretch sum is the difference of two prefix sums, and a difference is divisible by k exactly when the two prefix sums have the same remainder mod k. So the question becomes: do two prefix sums, at least two positions apart, share a remainder?

Scan once and store, for each remainder, the earliest prefix position where it appeared. Seed the map with remainder 0 at position 0 (the empty prefix), so a stretch starting at index 0 is found too. At each new prefix, if its remainder is already in the map and that position is at least 2 back, you found a stretch of length ≥ 2. Keeping the earliest position matters: it gives the longest stretch for that remainder, so you never miss one that is long enough.
steps: Create a map first with first[0] = 0 and a running sum s = 0.
For each index i, add nums[i] to s and compute rem = s mod k. This prefix covers positions 0..i, so it ends at position i + 1.
If rem is in the map and i + 1 − first[rem] ≥ 2, return true.
If rem is not in the map, store first[rem] = i + 1. Never overwrite an existing entry.
pitfalls: Overwriting the stored position with the latest one. In [3, 0] with k = 3 every prefix has remainder 0; if each replaces the last, every gap looks like 1 and the answer wrongly comes out false.
Forgetting the starting entry for remainder 0. Without it [2, 4] with k = 6 is missed, because the stretch starts at index 0.
Accepting a stretch of length one, such as the lone 6 in the second example.

solutions.title: Check every stretch
solutions.idea: Use prefix sums and try every pair of ends at least two apart.

solutions.title: Earliest position per remainder
solutions.idea: Two prefix sums with the same remainder bound a stretch divisible by k. Keep the earliest position of each remainder.

followups: Count how many stretches (of any length) have a sum divisible by k.
